content.title: About
content.content: Pollock is a cold‑water marine fish from the cod family, found in the North Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Raw pollock has a light pink to white flesh, a delicate flavor and a moderately firm texture. It is commonly used in sushi, sashimi and a variety of cooked dishes worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pollock is one of the fastest‑growing fish species, reaching market size in just 2–3 years.
Its meat is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart health.
In Japan, raw pollock is traditionally served as sashimi, sliced very thin.
Sustainable fisheries have helped restore pollock populations in the Atlantic.
Pollock is also processed into fish mince and protein powders.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help maintain cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Raw pollock provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in pollock is important for bone health and immune function.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Pollock supplies selenium, iodine and phosphorus, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Low heavy‑metal levels
items.content: When sourced responsibly, pollock typically contains low levels of mercury and other toxins.

items.title: Parasite risk
items.content: Raw fish may harbor parasites; freezing at –20 °C for at least 7 days is recommended before consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to marine fish.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: In certain regions pollock can be contaminated with heavy metals or pollutants; purchase from reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw pollock is sliced thin for sashimi, used in sushi rolls, or marinated in soy sauce with lemon or vinegar. Serve with fresh ginger, wasabi and soy sauce for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw pollock refrigerated at 0–2 °C, wrapped in plastic film or an airtight container. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C for at least 3 months. Before use, check for a fresh, non‑ammonia odor.
